answer: We prove Sybil resistance by coupling zero-knowledge delay functions with dynamic opportunity-cost bonds bound to a subgame-perfect slashing matrix. Indexing staking collateral to the systemic tide of network liquidity ensures identity multiplication incurs superlinear penalties, reducing the fable of cheap identities to strictly negative expected utility. The mechanism thus converges to a strict Nash equilibrium, where a willow graph of state dependencies guarantees that deviation costs strictly dominate any attack payoff.
